Type Description PointAccessResult

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For tilted_plane, whose planes have no rays toward the sky.

docs.title: Column post-processing
docs.text: column_postprocessing.py holds the column rules thresholding applies after the score threshold: carve_above_columns (the carve_above setting), carve_above_scores (for each voxel, the score cutoff below which carve_above removes it; thresholding uses it so that carve_fraction counts what carve_above removes) and limit_column_slope (the slope limit, max_slope_deg).

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.column_postprocessing
docs.text:
UrbanSolarCarver: column post-processing of the carved grid

Column rules applied by thresholding after the score threshold, so the kept volume is a buildable height field:

  • carve_above_columns / carve_above_scores: carve every occupied voxel above the lowest sufficiently-carved region of each (x, y) column (carve_above, carve_above_min_consecutive), on a boolean carve mask or directly on the scores.
  • limit_column_slope: cut columns that rise more steeply than max_slope_deg above a median-filtered height map, which turns one-voxel spires and tall cliffs into ramps. It only removes voxels.

The column loops are numba kernels.

docs.title: carve_above_columns(mask, voxel_grid, min_consecutive=1)
docs.text:
Carve occupied voxels above the lowest sufficiently-carved run per column.

For each (x, y) column, scans bottom-to-top (z=0 upward) for runs of consecutive carved voxels (occupied in voxel_grid, False in mask; empty cells break a run and never count as carved):

  • Runs with length >= min_consecutive trigger carve-above: all occupied voxels above the run are carved. The first (lowest) qualifying run triggers; scanning stops for that column.
  • Shorter runs do not trigger, but stay carved: the result only ever removes voxels, so it never re-violates the carving constraint.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mask ndarray (D, D, D) bool

Thresholding mask. True = keep, False = carved. Not mutated.

required voxel_grid ndarray (D, D, D) bool

Original envelope occupancy. True = occupied.

required min_consecutive int

Minimum consecutive carved voxels to trigger carve-above.

1

Returns:

Type Description ndarray (D, D, D) bool

A copy of mask with the occupied voxels above qualifying runs set to False.

docs.title: carve_above_scores(scores, occupancy, min_consecutive=1)
docs.text:
For each voxel, the score cutoff below which carve_above removes it.

Carving the occupied voxels that score above a cutoff t and then running :func:carve_above_columns removes exactly the occupied voxels whose value here is above t: a voxel goes when it scores above t itself, or when some run of min_consecutive consecutive occupied voxels below it in its column all score above t. So the value is the larger of the voxel's own score and, over those runs below it, the smallest score in the run. Empty cells break runs.

With these values a score-mass cutoff can count everything carve_above removes, not only the voxels the cutoff picks itself. NaN scores count as +inf (always carved).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default scores ndarray (X, Y, Z) float required occupancy ndarray (X, Y, Z) bool required min_consecutive int 1

Returns:

Type Description ndarray (X, Y, Z) float64

Values on empty cells are their own score and carry no meaning.

docs.title: limit_column_slope(mask, occupancy, max_slope_deg, median_size=5)
docs.text:
Lower columns that rise too steeply above their neighbours.

Each building column's kept height (one above its highest kept voxel, 0 if nothing is kept) is capped so that it rises at most tan(max_slope_deg) voxels per voxel of horizontal distance above a reference height map, counting the reference at the column itself as one voxel away; every kept voxel above the cap is removed. The result only ever removes voxels.

The reference is the kept height map after a median_size x median_size median filter over the building's columns, so features one or two columns wide are ignored: a single tall column (a spire) is measured against its surroundings and ends at most one slope step above them, and a single low column (a stub left at a curved edge) or a narrow slot does not pull its neighbours down. Wider differences in height, including next to areas carved to the ground, become ramps of the given slope, cut from the taller side. Columns outside the building (no occupied voxel) take no part.

The cap never rises when the input loses voxels, so carving more before this step never keeps more after it (a carve_fraction slider stays nested).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mask ndarray (X, Y, Z) bool

Kept voxels (True), normally after carve_above. Not mutated.

required occupancy ndarray (X, Y, Z) bool

The building's voxels before carving; decides which columns count.

required max_slope_deg float

Steepest allowed rise between neighbouring columns, in degrees above horizontal (0 < angle < 90; voxels are cubes, so the slope is the same in metres).

required median_size int

Width in voxels of the median filter that builds the reference.

5

Returns:

Type Description ndarray (X, Y, Z) bool

A copy of mask with the voxels above each column's cap removed.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Command-line interface built with Typer, installed as urbansolarcarver and its short alias usc. Provides the same 3-stage pipeline as the Python API, plus daemon management, config validation and introspection, and the simulated-weights tools.

# Run the whole pipeline
urbansolarcarver run -c config.yaml

# Produce the floor plates too, or reuse the scores and re-threshold
urbansolarcarver run -c config.yaml --produce exporting --produce massing
urbansolarcarver run -c config.yaml --start-from thresholding -o carve_fraction=0.5

# Run pipeline stages
urbansolarcarver preprocessing -c config.yaml
urbansolarcarver thresholding  -c config.yaml -f outputs/preprocessing/manifest.json
urbansolarcarver exporting     -c config.yaml -f outputs/thresholding/manifest.json

# Override any config value on the fly
urbansolarcarver preprocessing -c config.yaml -o voxel_size=0.5 -o mode=irradiance

# Check a config without running anything
urbansolarcarver validate -c config.yaml

# Build and validate a building archetype (prints derived areas)
urbansolarcarver archetype -o my_building.yaml -s width=12 -s wwr_south=0.4 -s mass_class=heavy

# Generate simulated benefit weights (writes simulated_weights.json + .png preview)
urbansolarcarver simulate-weights -e weather.epw -a my_building.yaml

# List the config parameters (optionally --mode benefit or --search threshold)
urbansolarcarver schema

# Precompile the Warp kernels
urbansolarcarver warmup

# Daemon lifecycle
urbansolarcarver daemon start
urbansolarcarver daemon status
urbansolarcarver daemon stop

Without -f, thresholding and exporting look for the previous stage's manifest.json under the config's out_dir.

run takes --produce (repeatable; preprocessing, thresholding, exporting or massing; default exporting) and runs the stages those need. --start-from (default preprocessing) skips the stages before it and reads their output from <out>/<stage>. Both work with --daemon, which sends the daemon's run command.

Issues noticed during a command (settings the mode ignores, nothing carved, ...) print after the result under Issues: as stage: code: message. A package error (an invalid config, an unusable input file, a missing or stale upstream output) prints Error: <message> and exits with 1, without a traceback.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.carver_cli
docs.text:
UrbanSolarCarver command-line interface.

Exposes the pipeline stages (preprocessing, thresholding, exporting, massing) as individual subcommands, plus run, which runs the stages needed for what --produce asks for (the carved mesh by default). Performance evaluation is out of scope: use Ladybug/Honeybee/Radiance on the exported mesh.

Utility commands: - warmup: precompile the Warp kernels once so the first run is not slow. - simulate-weights: build a simulated-weights file for benefit mode. - archetype: write and check a shoebox archetype YAML for simulate-weights. - validate: load and validate a YAML config without running anything. - schema: print a filterable parameter reference (by mode or keyword). - daemon: start / stop / status of the persistent GPU daemon used by Grasshopper and the --daemon flag on pipeline commands.

Design decisions ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ All heavy imports (torch, warp, api_core) are deferred to function bodies so that lightweight commands (--help, schema, validate, daemon) start quickly without initialising CUDA or compiling Warp kernels. Pipeline commands import urbansolarcarver.api inside their bodies, and the daemon commands use the standard-library daemon_client.

The --daemon flag on each pipeline command sends the job to a running daemon over localhost TCP (multiprocessing.connection), sharing the same RPC mechanism used by the Grasshopper plugin.

docs.title: main(ctx, version=Option(False, '--version', '-V', callback=_version_callback, is_eager=True, help='Show version and exit'), quiet=Option(False, '--quiet', '-q', help='Suppress torch/warp banners and non-essential output'))
docs.text: GPU-accelerated solar envelope generation for urban design.

docs.title: run(config=Option(..., '-c', '--config', exists=True, readable=True, help='YAML config path'), override=Option([], '-o', '--override', help='Override config KEY=VALUE'), out_dir=Option(None, '--out', help='Run folder (one subfolder per stage)'), produce=Option([], '--produce', help='Stage to produce: preprocessing, thresholding, exporting or massing (repeatable; default exporting)'), start_from=Option('preprocessing', '--start-from', help='First stage to run; the stage before it is read from the run folder'), daemon=Option(False, '--daemon', help='Send to running daemon instead of running locally'), quiet=Option(False, '-q', '--quiet', help='Minimal output'))
docs.text:
Run the stages needed to produce what --produce names.

With no --produce this chains preprocessing, thresholding and exporting into <out>/preprocessing, <out>/thresholding and <out>/exporting. --produce massing runs preprocessing, thresholding and massing; both together threshold once. With --start-from thresholding the scores already in <out>/preprocessing are reused, which is the way to iterate on threshold parameters without recomputing them.

A config with a criteria: list is a chain: the criteria are carved one after the other on one voxel grid, each deciding only among the voxels the one before kept, and exporting and massing build from the last. Each criterion's stages go to <out>/criteria/<id>/preprocessing and <out>/criteria/<id>/thresholding. --override then sets shared settings only (meshes, voxel size, out_dir, exporting, massing).

docs.title: cmd_preprocessing(config=Option(..., '-c', '--config', exists=True, readable=True, help='YAML config path'), override=Option([], '-o', '--override', help='Override config fields'), out_dir=Option(None, '--out', help='Output directory'), daemon=Option(False, '--daemon', help='Send to running daemon'), quiet=Option(False, '-q', '--quiet', help='Minimal output'), dry_run=Option(False, '--dry-run', help='Estimate grid size and memory, then exit without running'))
docs.text:
Voxelize, sample surfaces, trace rays, and write scores.

Outputs scores.npy, voxel_grid.npy, and manifest.json into the output directory. The manifest is consumed by the thresholding stage.

docs.title: cmd_thresholding(from_manifest=Option(None, '-f', '--from', help='Path to preprocessing manifest.json (auto-detected if omitted)'), config=Option(..., '-c', '--config', exists=True, readable=True, help='YAML config path'), override=Option([], '-o', '--override', help='Override config fields'), after=Option(None, '--after', exists=True, readable=True, help='Thresholding folder or manifest.json of the previous criterion: decide only among the voxels it kept'), out_dir=Option(None, '--out', help='Output directory'), daemon=Option(False, '--daemon', help='Send to running daemon'), quiet=Option(False, '-q', '--quiet', help='Minimal output'))
docs.text:
Apply the configured threshold to the preprocessing scores.

Reads the preprocessing manifest (-f) to locate scores.npy, applies the threshold from the config to the occupied voxels, and writes mask.npy (True = voxel kept).

This is the cheapest stage and is meant for quick iteration. Re-run with different -o threshold=... or -o carve_fraction=... values without recomputing scores.

With --after the threshold applies only to the voxels the previous criterion's thresholding kept (one step of a chain; run does the whole chain from a config with criteria:).

docs.title: cmd_exporting(from_manifest=Option(None, '-f', '--from', help='Path to thresholding manifest.json (auto-detected if omitted)'), config=Option(..., '-c', '--config', exists=True, readable=True, help='YAML config path'), override=Option([], '-o', '--override', help='Override config fields'), out_dir=Option(None, '--out', help='Output directory'), daemon=Option(False, '--daemon', help='Send to running daemon'), quiet=Option(False, '-q', '--quiet', help='Minimal output'))
docs.text:
Reconstruct a triangle mesh from the binary carving mask.

Reads the thresholding manifest (-f) to locate mask.npy, prunes small disconnected clusters, reconstructs a triangle mesh (cubic faces or SDF-smoothed marching cubes), and writes export.<format> (format from final_mesh_format, default ply).

docs.title: cmd_massing(from_manifest=Option(None, '-f', '--from', help='Path to thresholding manifest.json (auto-detected if omitted)'), config=Option(..., '-c', '--config', exists=True, readable=True, help='YAML config path'), override=Option([], '-o', '--override', help='Override config fields'), out_dir=Option(None, '--out', help='Output directory'), daemon=Option(False, '--daemon', help='Send to running daemon'), quiet=Option(False, '-q', '--quiet', help='Minimal output'))
docs.text:
Build stacked floor plates that follow the footprint, from the carving mask.

Reads the thresholding manifest (-f) and writes plates.json (outlines in world coordinates) and plates.obj (one closed prism per plate), and the same plates as plates.<format> when final_mesh_format is not obj. Settings: ground_floor_height, floor_height, min_plate_dimension, plate_tolerance, plate_stacking, final_mesh_format.

docs.title: warmup(device=Option('auto', '--device', '-d', help="Target device: 'auto', 'cpu', or 'cuda'"))
docs.text:
Compile the Warp compute kernels ahead of time.

Warp compiles kernels just in time on first use, a one-time cost of roughly 3-10 s per machine, device and code version that is cached on disk afterwards. Run this once after installing or updating UrbanSolarCarver so the first carving run reflects real compute time. (setup_env.py and the daemon do this automatically.) Exits with code 1 if the Warp backend is not available on the device.

docs.title: simulate_weights(epw=Option(..., '-e', '--epw', exists=True, readable=True, help='EPW weather file'), archetype=Option(..., '-a', '--archetype', exists=True, readable=True, help='Archetype YAML (see configs/archetype_example.yaml)'), out=Option(Path('simulated_weights.json'), '-o', '--out', help='Output artifact path'), eps=Option(1.0, '--eps', help='Perturbation size in W (central differences)'))
docs.text:
Write a simulated-weights file for benefit mode.

Runs the ISO 13790 Annex C simple hourly model (5R1C: five resistances, one capacitance) for the archetype and weather file, perturbs the solar gain by +/- eps W each hour, and records the hourly marginal benefit and harm of solar gain (central differences).

The file is read through benefit mode's simulated_weights_path config key, where it replaces the balance-point on/off hour filter with these hourly weights. See design/simulated-weights.md.

docs.title: archetype(out=Option(Path('archetype.yaml'), '-o', '--out', help='Output archetype YAML path'), set_=Option([], '-s', '--set', help='Override a field, e.g. -s width=12 -s wwr_south=0.4 -s mass_class=heavy'), from_=Option(None, '--from', help='Start from an existing shoebox archetype YAML instead of defaults'), force=Option(False, '--force', help='Overwrite the output file if it exists'))
docs.text:
Build a shoebox archetype, validate it, and report derived quantities.

The file is validated through the same code path the generator uses (expand_shoebox + ZoneParams.from_archetype) before writing, and the derived floor area, volume, and per-facade window areas are printed so mistakes surface here rather than inside a simulation.

Only the shoebox form is built by this command; explicit-area archetypes are edited directly in YAML (see configs/archetype_example.yaml).

docs.title: validate(config=Option(..., '-c', '--config', exists=True, readable=True, help='YAML config path'), override=Option([], '-o', '--override', help='Override config fields'))
docs.text:
Parse and validate the YAML config through Pydantic.

Exits with code 1 if the config fails schema or value checks. Missing mesh (context and terrain included), EPW and simulated-weights files, and a simulated-weights file that cannot be read, are printed as warnings only (exit code 0). Does not initialise CUDA or import torch.

A config with a criteria: list is a chain: every criterion is validated and listed on a line of its own, with the settings the criteria share printed once.

docs.title: schema(mode=Option(None, '--mode', '-m', help='Show only parameters relevant to this mode'), search=Option(None, '--search', '-s', help='Filter parameters by name or description substring'))
docs.text:
Print the full UserConfig parameter table.

Reads field metadata from the Pydantic schema, so no heavy imports are needed. Filter by mode (--mode benefit) to see only the parameters that mode uses, or search by keyword (--search threshold).

docs.title: ui(port=Option(UI_DEFAULT_PORT, '--port', help='Port on 127.0.0.1'), projects_folder=Option(None, '--projects-folder', help='Folder that holds one subfolder per project (default: the folder chosen in the app, else ~/UrbanSolarCarver/projects)'), no_browser=Option(False, '--no-browser', help='Print the address without opening the browser'), device=Option('auto', '--device', '-d', help="Compute device: 'auto', 'cpu', or 'cuda'"))
docs.text:
Start the local web service and open the interface in the default browser.

The service listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Each launch creates a random token, which the browser receives once in the address and sends with every request; the address is printed here as well. The compute kernels are compiled in the background while the interface is used. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

docs.title: daemon_start(foreground=Option(False, '-F', '--foreground', help='Run daemon in this console (blocks)'), python=Option(None, '--python', help='Python interpreter to use for the daemon process'))
docs.text:
Start the GPU daemon as a detached background process.

Does nothing if a daemon already answers on the port. Detached runs use pythonw.exe on Windows (no console window, unless --python is given) and write their output to ~/.urbansolarcarver/daemon.log, which is overwritten on each start. -F runs in this console instead, which is useful for debugging. A detached start polls once per second, for up to 30 s, until the daemon answers a ping, and exits with code 1 if it does not.

docs.text: Send a shutdown command to the running daemon.

docs.title: daemon_status()
docs.text: Ping the daemon and print its pid; exit with code 1 if it does not answer.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
USC uses YAML files for all pipeline parameters. The configuration system provides:

  • Typed values through build_config, for clients that hold values rather than a file (Grasshopper through the daemon).
  • YAML loading of a flat mapping of settings; an analysis_period: mapping with Ladybug AnalysisPeriod.to_dict() keys is expanded into the six period fields. Relative paths are resolved against the YAML file's folder.
  • Overrides (-o key=value on the CLI, or a mapping in Python) that replace top-level values from the file.
  • Pydantic v2 validation with value ranges, type coercion, rejection of unknown keys, and one error message listing every problem. Both entry points raise ConfigError, whose errors list gives the field and message of each problem.
  • Chain files: a YAML with a criteria: list is loaded by load_chain into a ChainConfig (see Criteria); load_config refuses it and is_chain_file(path) tells the two apart.
  • Manifest schemas for the preprocessing and thresholding stages, so a later stage can be re-run from an earlier run's output.

See also: Configuration guide for the user-facing parameter reference.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.load_config
docs.text:
Load a YAML config, apply overrides, and validate it into a user_config.

Overrides come from the CLI (key=value strings), the daemon, or Grasshopper. :func:build_config validates already-typed values (no YAML involved) and raises a structured :class:~urbansolarcarver.errors.ConfigError. The schema itself lives in :mod:pydantic_schemas.

docs.title: parse_override_value(raw)
docs.text:
Convert a key=value override's value into a Python value.

"true"/"false" become bool and "null"/"none" None (case-insensitive); JSON lists and objects are parsed ([45,40,35]), then int, then float; anything else stays a string. "inf" and "nan" stay strings so the schema reports them clearly.

parse_override_value("true") True parse_override_value("3.5") 3.5 parse_override_value("foofoo") 'foofoo'

docs.title: Chain config
docs.text: Shared settings are at the top level of a chain file and each criterion's own settings are listed under criteria:. load_chain(path, overrides) returns a ChainConfig: criteria is a tuple of Criterion(id, name, config) with one validated config per criterion, and shared is the last criterion's config. A criterion's id (default: its position from 1) names its output folder, so it is 1 to 40 letters, digits, _ or -, unique ignoring case and not a Windows device name (CON, NUL, COM1, ...). A shared setting inside a criterion, or a criterion setting at the top level or in -o overrides, is an error that names the setting; chain_config.CRITERION_KEYS lists the criterion settings.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.chain_config
docs.text:
The criteria: form of a config: several criteria carved in sequence on one voxel grid.

A chain file sets the shared settings once at the top level (meshes, voxel size, weather file, output folder, exporting and massing) and lists the settings of each criterion under criteria: (mode, test surface, how the voxels are decided, the mode's own parameters, its analysis period). :func:load_chain turns it into one validated user_config per criterion, so everything downstream reads ordinary configs.

docs.title: ChainConfig(criteria, shared) dataclass
docs.text: A chain of criteria. shared is the last criterion's config: exporting and massing read their settings from it, and those are all shared keys, equal in every criterion.

docs.title: Criterion(id, name, config) dataclass
docs.text: One criterion of a chain: its id (also its folder name), its display name and its validated config.

docs.title: load_chain(path, overrides=None)
docs.text:
Load the chain file at path, apply overrides, and validate each criterion.

Each criterion's config is the shared settings plus its own, without the weather file when its mode does not read one. A criterion's id (default: its position from 1) names its output folder; its name (default: its mode) is for display.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

YAML file with a criteria: list. Relative paths in it (top level and criteria) are resolved against the file's folder.

required overrides list[str] | Mapping[str, Any] | None

Top-level settings that replace the YAML's: "key=value" strings or a mapping, as for :func:~urbansolarcarver.load_config.load_config. Shared settings only: a criterion setting in the overrides is refused.

None

Raises:

Type Description FileNotFoundError

If path does not exist.

ConfigError

On malformed YAML, a file without criteria, a shared setting inside a criterion, a criterion setting at the top level, an id that is repeated, unsafe as a folder name or reserved by Windows, or an invalid criterion (the message starts criterion <id> (<name>):).

docs.title: is_chain_file(path)
docs.text: Whether the YAML at path is a mapping with a criteria key. A missing or malformed file is not a chain file; loading it reports the problem.

docs.title: Mode starting values
docs.text: mode_registry.MODES holds one ModeSpec per carving mode. Its starting_values are the settings that differ from the schema defaults and fill a new config for the mode: the analysis period of time-based, irradiance and benefit, tilted_plane_angle_deg: 45 for tilted_plane and carve_fraction: 0.35 for radiative_cooling. A client with no YAML file (Grasshopper through the daemon's run command) gets its config from these values plus its overrides. The schema defaults and validation rules are unchanged, so a CLI config without carve_fraction keeps 0.7 in every mode and time-based still requires an analysis period. The files in configs/ repeat the starting values as commented examples. ModeSpec.description is the text the Grasshopper mode component shows, MODE_ALIASES lists the accepted spellings (time_based, tilted-plane, ...) and canonical_mode_name(name) maps a name to the canonical one.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.pydantic_schemas
docs.text:
Pydantic schemas for YAML configuration validation and stage manifests.

Defines :class:UserConfig (the pipeline configuration model, imported elsewhere as user_config), :class:ThresholdSpec (the normalized threshold setting), the four stage manifest schemas (:class:PreprocessingManifest, :class:ThresholdingManifest, :class:ExportingManifest, :class:MassingManifest) and the project-specific warning class :class:UrbanSolarCarverWarning.

The config schemas use extra='forbid' so that typos in YAML keys are caught at load time rather than silently ignored. The manifest schemas use Pydantic's default and ignore unknown keys.

docs.title: ThresholdSpec
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Canonical thresholding strategy: how per-voxel scores become a mask.

Every accepted config spelling of threshold (a bare number, a strategy name, or a mapping) is normalized into this one shape at load time, so downstream stages never re-interpret raw user input.

Methods:

Name Description * ``carve_fraction``: carve the highest-scoring voxels that together

hold value (0-1) of the total score mass.

* ``headtail``: head/tail breaks * ``cutoff``: carve voxels scoring strictly above ``value``; for

time-based this is the tolerated shading in m²·h.

docs.title: threshold_reads_carve_fraction(threshold)
docs.text:
Whether a threshold, in any spelling the config accepts, takes its value from carve_fraction.

It does when unset (in a weighted mode) or when it names the carve_fraction method without a value. A spelling the schema refuses reads nothing here; validation reports it.

docs.title: resolve_threshold(mode, threshold, carve_fraction)
docs.text:
The complete thresholding strategy for mode.

threshold is the config's field as written: None takes the mode default (carve_fraction with the carve_fraction value for the weighted modes, cutoff 0 for the violation-count modes), and carve_fraction without a value takes carve_fraction. Raises ValueError for a method the mode cannot use: violation-count scores take only a cutoff, and tilted_plane only cutoff 0.

docs.title: resolve_max_slope_deg(mode, max_slope_deg)
docs.text:
The slope limit thresholding applies for mode, or None when it is off.

An explicit max_slope_deg applies as given (90 = off). Unset, it is 75 degrees for the weighted modes, whose per-voxel score cutoffs can leave cliffs and spires, and off for the violation-count modes (time-based, tilted_plane), whose results follow the rays exactly.

docs.title: resolve_grid_step(grid_step, voxel_size)
docs.text:
The sample spacing on the test surfaces, in meters: grid_step as given, or half the voxel size when it is unset.

Measured on the district example (Solar usefulness, 1 m voxels), half the voxel size keeps the kept voxels within about 1 % of a 0.25 m reference at about twice the time of a spacing of one voxel (2 %).

docs.title: expand_analysis_period(data)
docs.text:
Expand an analysis_period mapping into the six flat period fields.

Canonical form uses Ladybug's AnalysisPeriod.to_dict() keys (st_month ... end_hour), so a Ladybug period can be pasted or passed directly; start_month-style keys work as well. Returns a new dict. Raises ValueError if analysis_period is not a mapping, has an unknown key, or disagrees with a flat period field in the same dict.

docs.title: Daemon
docs.text:
A persistent background process that keeps a CarverSession (and with it the CUDA context and the compiled Warp kernels) alive for low-latency calls from Grasshopper or other clients. It communicates via Python's multiprocessing.connection over localhost; clients authenticate with a random key stored in ~/.urbansolarcarver/.daemon_authkey.

The daemon is started and stopped via the CLI (urbansolarcarver daemon start/stop, daemon status to check it) or from within Grasshopper using the USC_Session component. It binds to 127.0.0.1 only and is not reachable from the network.

docs.title: A transport over the engine requests
docs.text:
The daemon only carries messages. Each request is a dict with a cmd key; the daemon passes it to engine_requests.answer_engine_message, which runs it and returns the reply dict, with status "ok" or "error". The commands, their keys and their replies are described in Engine requests. The daemon itself handles one more command, shutdown, which stops it.

Clients reach it through daemon_client.py, which uses only the standard library: resolve_daemon_authkey reads (or creates) the key and send_daemon_request sends one request, so asking the daemon something does not load torch. Grasshopper keeps its own copy of the key reading in usc_gh.py, because Rhino's Python does not import this package.

A message the daemon cannot unpickle gets an error reply too, and the daemon keeps running. Failed requests are logged with their traceback in the daemon's console or log file.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.daemon
docs.text:
Long-running server that keeps a GPU session alive between pipeline calls.

Used by the Grasshopper components and the CLI --daemon flag. Starts a single CarverSession and listens on a multiprocessing.connection Listener for request dicts such as {"cmd": "run", "produce": [...], ...}. The daemon is a transport: each request goes to :func:urbansolarcarver.engine_requests.answer_engine_message, which runs it and returns the reply dict ("status" is "ok" or "error") that is sent back. Only shutdown is handled here, since it stops the transport.

Security assumptions
  • Localhost only: the daemon binds to the loopback interface. Host names that do not resolve to 127.0.0.1 or ::1 are rejected at startup.
  • Authkey: 32 random bytes, stored as 64 hex characters in ~/.urbansolarcarver/.daemon_authkey, are generated on first use. Clients must present this key.
  • Pickle IPC: multiprocessing.connection uses pickle internally. Any process that holds the authkey can execute arbitrary code in the daemon's context. This is acceptable because both endpoints run on the same machine under the same user account.
  • Not designed for multi-user or server deployment. Do not expose the daemon port to a network.

docs.title: serve(address, authkey, device_arg='auto')
docs.text:
Serve pipeline requests from Grasshopper and the CLI until "shutdown".

Keeps one CarverSession (CUDA context and compiled Warp kernels) alive across requests. The commands are those of :mod:engine_requests, plus shutdown. Requests are handled one at a time; a failing request becomes an error reply and the server keeps running.

docs.title: Engine requests
docs.text:
urbansolarcarver.engine_requests turns a request message into an engine call and a reply. Every transport uses it: the daemon today, a local HTTP service later. It does not import torch until a request runs.

  • parse_engine_request(message) validates a dict into one of the request models below, or raises MalformedEngineRequest (a ValueError) when the message is not a dict, names an unknown command, or lacks or misuses a key.
  • config_for_engine_request(request) builds the config: from the YAML file in config with overrides on top, or, without a file, from the starting values of the mode the overrides name (load_config.build_config_from_mode_starting_values).
  • handle_engine_request(request, session, context=None) runs the request inside a run context and returns a reply model; engine errors propagate. A given RunContext receives progress, issues and cancellation.
  • answer_engine_message(message, session) does all of this for transports that carry dicts and never raises: any failure becomes an error reply.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
run runs the stages needed to produce produce, through the same sequencer as run_pipeline().

Request key Meaning produce List of stages to produce: preprocessing, thresholding, exporting, massing run_folder The folder that holds one subfolder per stage start_from First stage to run (default preprocessing); earlier stages are read from run_folder config Optional path of a YAML config overrides Optional list of key=value strings, or a mapping trace_criteria Chain files only: list of criterion ids to trace again when starting from preprocessing; the others reuse their existing preprocessing. Default: all threshold_from_criterion Chain files only: the id of the criterion thresholding starts at. With trace_criteria it applies when that criterion comes before the first traced one (its preprocessing is read as it is); with start_from: "thresholding" the criteria before it keep their thresholding folders. Default: thresholding starts at the first traced criterion, or at the first criterion when nothing is traced after Configs without criteria: only, with start_from thresholding: the previous criterion's thresholding folder or manifest.json, passed to thresholding as after. A chain file, or a run that starts anywhere else, gets a ConfigError reply. Default: none

When config is a chain file (a criteria: list), run runs the chain through run_chain and overrides set the shared settings only; run_folder then holds criteria/<id>/..., exporting and massing (see Criteria). The reply's stage_folders and manifest point at the last criterion's folders and at the chain's exporting and massing. With trace_criteria, every criterion from the first traced one on is thresholded again; the ones before it keep their thresholding, unless threshold_from_criterion names an earlier one, from which thresholding then starts. With start_from: "thresholding", every criterion is thresholded again unless threshold_from_criterion names one; thresholding then starts there and reads the earlier criteria's thresholding folders (a missing one is a StageChainError naming it).

Without config, the config is built in memory from the starting values of the mode named in the overrides (mode is required) with the overrides on top; no file is written.

The reply holds stage_folders (stage name to folder, only for the stages that ran in this call), manifest (the manifest of the last of them), issues, and export_path (exporting), plates_path, mesh_path (the OBJ) and export_mesh_path (the plates in final_mesh_format) (massing) for the stages that produced them.

preprocessing, thresholding, exporting, massing run one stage. They need config; every stage but preprocessing also needs from, the upstream stage's folder or manifest. out_dir defaults to <config out_dir>/<stage>. thresholding also takes after, the previous criterion's thresholding folder or manifest.json (StageRequest.after): the stage then decides only among the voxels that criterion kept, and out_dir may not be that criterion's own folder. The reply has issues and manifest, export_path (exporting) or plates_path, mesh_path and export_mesh_path (massing).

run_pipeline runs preprocessing, thresholding and exporting into out_dir (default: the config's out_dir); Grasshopper definitions saved before run existed still send it. simulate_weights writes a simulated-weights file (epw, archetype, out, optional internal_gains_w_m2 and eps) and replies with artifact and preview. ping replies with the process id (pid) and features, a list of what this engine supports beyond the first version (run_after: the after key of run), so a client can tell an older engine.

check runs one Simulate study: the sun and sky check (solar_check.simulate_study) of a test surface file against the project's geometries, written to out_dir. It samples the test surface in the maximum volume's local frame (its minimum corner rounded to 1 µm, as preprocessing does) and traces every sun or sky direction against each geometry with Warp, without a carving run.

Request key Meaning test_surface_path The mesh file of the test surfaces max_volume_path The mesh file of the maximum volume out_dir Where check_summary.json, check_points.npz and check_values.npz are written settings CheckSettings values (metric, the period, sample_spacing, rays_per_patch, ...); an invalid one is a ConfigError reply run_folder Optional run folder: its built envelope (exporting) and massing are added as columns, found through their manifests and clipped by the maximum volume. A manifest that exists but cannot be read or names no mesh leaves its geometry out, with the issue geometry_manifest_unusable naming the geometry and the file context_path, terrain_path Optional mesh files that block in every column; a file without triangles is ignored with an issue voxel_size Surface tolerance of the envelope and massing when the run folder does not record the voxel size they were built with (default 1.0) device auto (default), cpu or cuda

The columns are open (no geometry), max_volume, then envelope and massing when built; the summary compares them with max_volume. Progress is reported per kernel launch under the stage check, and a cancel raises RunCancelled between launches. More than 2 million test points (solar_check.MAX_CHECK_POINTS, estimated from the test surfaces' area and sample_spacing) is an InputError naming the spacing that fits. The summary records under fingerprints what the result was computed from: test_surface, max_volume, geometries (the envelope's and massing's meshes, only those built), weather (only for a metric that reads it), context and terrain (each {path, size, modified_ns}, or null) and settings_digest (sha256 of the settings' JSON, sorted keys, without epw_path, which weather records), so a client can tell that a result is out of date. The reply has summary_path and issues.

Keys a command does not use are ignored. Reply fields that are None are left out.

docs.title: Replies
docs.text: Every reply to a run or stage command has issues, a list of {stage, code, message}. An error reply has error (the text), error_type (the exception class name; MalformedEngineRequest for a malformed request) and, for a ConfigError, config_errors, a list of {field, message}.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.engine_requests
docs.text:
Requests the engine answers, shared by every transport.

A transport (the pickle daemon today, an HTTP service later) receives a message; this module turns it into an engine call and a reply:

  • :func:parse_engine_request validates a message into one of the request models, or raises :class:~urbansolarcarver.errors.MalformedEngineRequest.
  • :func:config_for_engine_request builds the request's config: from its YAML file with the overrides on top or, without a file, from the starting values of the mode the overrides name.
  • :func:handle_engine_request runs a request inside a run context and returns a reply model; engine errors propagate to the caller.
  • :func:error_reply_for turns an exception into an error reply.
  • :func:answer_engine_message does all of this for transports that carry plain dicts, and never raises.

Stopping a transport is the transport's own business, not a request here. Importing this module does not import torch: the stage functions are imported when a request runs.

docs.title: RunRequest
docs.text:
Bases: _EngineRequest

Run the stages needed to produce produce in run_folder (:func:urbansolarcarver.api.run_pipeline). Without config (a YAML path) the overrides must name the mode. When config is a chain file (a criteria: list) the request runs :func:urbansolarcarver.api.run_chain and the overrides set shared settings only. trace_criteria (chain only, ignored otherwise) lists the criterion ids to trace again when starting from preprocessing; the others reuse their existing preprocessing. threshold_from_criterion (chain only) names the criterion thresholding starts at: with trace_criteria, one that comes before the first traced one; when starting from thresholding, any one, the criteria before it keeping their thresholding. after (a config without criteria:, a run that starts at thresholding) is the previous criterion's thresholding folder or manifest: thresholding then decides only among the voxels that criterion kept. A chain file or an earlier start_from refuses it.

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text:
The geometry pipeline from raw meshes to the output mesh, in three modules:

  1. Surface sampling (surface_sampling.py): discretizes test-surface faces into evenly spaced points with outward-facing normals, using grid_step and a coplanarity tolerance; also computes the edge_taper weights. Used by preprocessing.
  2. Voxelization (voxelization.py): converts the max-volume mesh into a dense cubic boolean grid at the configured voxel_size. Used by preprocessing.
  3. Meshing (meshing.py): removes voxel clusters smaller than min_voxels and converts the carved voxel mask back into a triangle mesh, either as cubic voxel faces or via SDF smoothing + marching cubes + Taubin polishing. Used by exporting.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.surface_sampling
docs.text:
UrbanSolarCarver: test-surface sampling

Samples the test surfaces into the points and normals that rays start from, and the analysis-mesh quads that show one face per sample point. Used by preprocessing.

Pipeline entry point

sample_surface(insolation_mesh, settings) discretize_surface_with_normals with the preprocessing settings; raises when no sample points are produced.

Public API

sample_planar_surface(mesh, sample_step=1.0, include_boundary=True, edge_taper=0.0) Sample one planar connected component on a regular grid. Returns points, normals, analysis-mesh quads (vertices + faces), and edge-taper weights.

discretize_surface_with_normals(mesh, sample_step=1.0, coplanarity_tol_deg=5.0, edge_taper=0.0) Split the mesh into connected components, sample each planar one, and return points, normals, an AnalysisMesh, weights, and taper statistics.

AnalysisMesh Quad mesh with one face per sample point; serialised to analysis_mesh.json.

Internal helpers

plane_frame(surface_normal) Orthonormal in-plane basis for planar sampling.

_mesh_boundary_loops(mesh), _sample_boundary_edges(polygon, ...) Boundary extraction and extra samples along boundary edges.

Data types and units
  • Points and normals: np.ndarray, shape (N, 3), world units.

docs.title: AnalysisMesh(vertices, faces, face_normals=None)
docs.text:
One quad per sample point: the patch of test surface each point stands for.

Written to analysis_mesh.json by preprocessing, for visualising sampling density or per-point results.

Attributes:

Name Type Description vertices (V, 3) float64 array of quad corners faces (N, 4) int32 array of quad vertex indices, one quad per sample point face_normals (N, 3) float32 array of outward unit normals, or None

docs.title: to_dict()
docs.text: Serialise to a plain dict (vertices + faces as nested lists).

docs.title: sample_surface(insolation_mesh, settings)
docs.text:

docs.title: plane_frame(surface_normal)
docs.text:
Return two orthonormal vectors spanning the plane orthogonal to surface_normal.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default surface_normal (3,) array_like

Plane normal (need not be unit length).

required

Returns:

Type Description axis_u, axis_v : (3,) np.ndarray

Unit vectors with cross(axis_u, axis_v) equal to the unit normal, so (axis_u, axis_v, normal) is a right-handed frame.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If surface_normal has near-zero length.

Notes
  • The normal is normalized internally.
  • The reference axis is X, or Y when the normal is within about 26 deg of X, so the cross product never degenerates.
  • The result depends only on the normal, so panels with the same normal get the same frame (up to the sign of axis_u when the normal is negated).
  • Used by sample_planar_surface to build a local 2D sampling frame.

docs.title: sample_planar_surface(mesh, sample_step=1.0, include_boundary=True, edge_taper=0.0)
docs.text:
Sample points on a regular grid over one planar submesh.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh Trimesh

Single planar connected component (convex or not, with or without holes).

required sample_step float

Spacing of the sampling grid in world units.

1.0 include_boundary bool

If True, keep grid points that fall on the polygon boundary; otherwise drop them. Extra points seeded along the boundary edges (_sample_boundary_edges) are added in both cases.

True edge_taper float

Design-constraint taper distance (world units). When > 0, each sample gets a weight ramping linearly from 0 at the component outline (exterior and holes) to 1 at edge_taper from it.

0.0

Returns:

Name Type Description points (N, 3) float64 np.ndarray

Sample locations in world coordinates.

normals (N, 3) np.ndarray

Unit normal, the same for every point, oriented to agree with the area-weighted normal of the mesh faces.

quad_verts (4N, 3) float64 np.ndarray

Corner positions of one analysis-mesh quad per sample point.

quad_faces (N, 4) int32 np.ndarray

Vertex indices of each quad (indices into quad_verts).

weights (N,) float32 np.ndarray

Edge-taper design weights in [0, 1]; all ones when edge_taper == 0.

Notes

  • If no grid site falls inside the polygon, one point guaranteed to lie inside it (Shapely's representative_point) is used as the single sample.
  • Used by discretize_surface_with_normals for planar-only sampling.

docs.title: discretize_surface_with_normals(mesh, sample_step=1.0, coplanarity_tol_deg=5.0, edge_taper=0.0)
docs.text:
Sample the nearly planar connected components of a mesh and return point/normal pairs.

Each connected component whose faces all lie within coplanarity_tol_deg of the component's area-weighted mean normal is sampled with sample_planar_surface; other components are skipped with a UserWarning. The quad analysis mesh has one face per sample point, suitable for per-face colouring (e.g. "LB Spatial Heatmap" in Grasshopper/Rhino).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh Trimesh

Input triangle mesh (test surface).

required sample_step float

Sampling grid spacing in world units.

1.0 coplanarity_tol_deg float

Maximum face-normal deviation (degrees) to consider a component planar.

5.0 edge_taper float

Design-constraint taper distance (meters): sample weights ramp from 0 at each component's outline to 1 at edge_taper inward. Distances are measured in the component's plane, which the coplanarity check guarantees exists.

0.0

Returns:

Name Type Description points (N, 3) float32 np.ndarray

Sample points (centroids of the analysis-mesh quads).

normals (N, 3) float32 np.ndarray

Outward-facing normals at each sample point.

analysis_mesh AnalysisMesh or None

Combined quad analysis mesh, or None if no points were sampled.

Edge-taper design weights in [0, 1]; all ones when edge_taper == 0.

Per-component taper statistics (empty when edge_taper == 0). Components that never reach full weight (narrower than ~2× the taper) also emit a UserWarning, so the user knows that geometry is partly or wholly excluded from the protected program.

UrbanSolarCarver: voxelization

Rasterizes the maximum volume into a padded cubic occupancy grid. Used by preprocessing.

Pipeline entry point

Public API

voxelize_mesh(mesh, voxel_size=1.0, margin_frac=0.2, device=None) Rasterize a watertight mesh into a padded cubic occupancy grid. The result is cached in the active CarverSession under a key made of the mesh arrays, voxel size, margin and device (_voxelize_cache_key).

voxelize_solid_warp(vertices, faces, grid_origin, voxel_size, resolution, device) The Warp parity voxelizer voxelize_mesh uses (kernel in warp_kernels); None when Warp cannot run on the device.

Data types and units
  • Voxel grids: torch.Tensor, shape (D, D, D), uint8/bool, 1 = inside.
  • voxel_size is in world units.

docs.text:
Rasterize a watertight mesh into a padded binary voxel grid.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh Trimesh required voxel_size float

Edge length of one voxel in world units.

1.0 margin_frac float

Padding on each side as a fraction of the longest side of the mesh's axis-aligned bounding box.

0.2 device device or None

Device for the returned tensor and for the Warp voxelizer; None picks CUDA when available, else CPU.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description voxels (D, D, D) uint8 torch.Tensor

1 where inside/filled, 0 otherwise.

origin (3,) np.ndarray

World-space min corner of the grid.

grid_extent float

Side length of the cubic domain in world units (D * voxel_size).

resolution int

Number of voxels per side (D).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If voxel_size <= 0, margin_frac < 0, or the grid would have more than grid_planning.MAX_GRID_VOXELS voxels (checked before anything is allocated).

RuntimeError

If the Warp voxelizer fails (for example out of memory), or the trimesh voxelization fails.

Notes
  • Uses the Warp parity voxelizer (voxelize_solid_warp below, on CUDA or the Warp CPU device); only when Warp cannot run on device does it use trimesh voxelization plus fill. Sealed interior cavities are then filled with scipy's binary_fill_holes.
  • The grid is axis-aligned, cubic, and centred on the mesh bounding box.
  • Results are cached per session (see _voxelize_cache_key).

docs.title: voxelize_solid_warp(vertices, faces, grid_origin, voxel_size, resolution, device, *, centre_only=False, span_min=None, span_max=None)
docs.text:
Solid-voxelize a triangle mesh by parity ray casting along x, y and z against a Warp BVH (bounding volume hierarchy).

A voxel is occupied when at least 2 of the 3 axis parity tests find its centre inside (a majority vote, so one axis confused by a small hole or a grazing ray does not decide the result; trimesh's orthographic fill uses the same idea), or when the mesh surface passes through it. Runs on CUDA or the Warp CPU device; voxelization.py uses trimesh's slower rasterize-and-fill only when this returns None, and lets anything it raises propagate.

With centre_only the surface-through rule is left out: a voxel is occupied only when its centre is inside (the context rule). span_min and span_max (same frame as grid_origin) move the start and end of the per-axis rays out to them where they lie beyond the grid, so a mesh larger than the grid keeps a correct parity inside it; votes are still written only for cells of the grid. The defaults give the maximum volume's voxelization unchanged.

Returns:

Type Description ndarray | None

(resolution, resolution, resolution) bool occupancy array, or None when the Warp backend is unavailable on device.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the mesh has no vertices or no faces.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.meshing
docs.text:
UrbanSolarCarver: meshing

Cleans the carved occupancy grid and turns it into the output mesh. Used by exporting.

Overview

Two meshing modes are supported:

1) Cubic (apply_smoothing == False) - Clean the binary grid: drop small connected components, then drop occupied voxels with fewer than 2 occupied neighbours in their 3×3×3 neighbourhood. - Triangulate with the shared-vertex cubic mesher (_cubic_mesh_from_occupancy).

2) Smoothed SDF (apply_smoothing == True) - Convert occupancy to a signed distance field (SDF) in voxel units. - Light Gaussian blur, then edge-preserving Perona–Malik diffusion; the result is kept only within 2 voxels of the zero level. - Pick an iso value that preserves the original inside volume. - Extract a surface with marching cubes (scikit-image). - Optionally run a short Taubin polish (0 to 6 iterations) after cleanup.

Pipeline entry point

finalize_mesh(carved_grid, grid_origin, settings, voxel_size) Clean the carved grid and mesh it with the cubic or smoothed path.

Public API

prune_voxels(voxels, min_voxels) Remove 26-connected components smaller than min_voxels.

prune_voxels_morph(voxels, min_voxels) Cleanup for the cubic path: component prune, then the neighbour-count filter described above. Only removes voxels; no erosion or closing.

mesh_from_voxels(voxels, min_corner, voxel_size) Build a blocky mesh from the binary grid. Returns an unprocessed Trimesh.

mesh_from_voxels_smoothed(voxels, min_corner, voxel_size) Build a smooth mesh by contouring a smoothed SDF with marching cubes. Uses a volume-matched iso to avoid systematic thinning.

cleanup_mesh(mesh, min_face_count=100, light=False) Fix winding/normals (unless light), weld vertices, drop small fragments.

polish_mesh_taubin(mesh, iters=2) Optional Taubin polish after the SDF + marching cubes path, at most 6 iterations.

Internal helpers

_cubic_mesh_from_occupancy(voxels, min_corner, voxel_size) Vertex and face arrays for the cubic mesher.

_voxel_presmooth(field_bool) SDF build + Gaussian + narrow-band Perona–Malik diffusion.

_pm_anisotropic_diffuse(sdf, iters, k, tau) Edge-preserving diffusion stepper used by _voxel_presmooth.

_volume_matched_threshold(sdf, target_inside_voxels) Iso selection that matches the original inside count.

_median_edge_length(m) Median of unique edge lengths; used to normalize the Taubin polish.

Data types and units
  • Voxel grids: torch.Tensor, shape (D, D, D), uint8/bool, 1 = inside.
  • Meshes: trimesh.Trimesh in world coordinates.
  • voxel_size is in world units and is passed to marching cubes as the grid spacing.
Notes
  • The cubic path gives a blocky "voxel look" that is stable between runs. It applies no erosion, so thin volumes are kept.
  • The smoothed path operates in SDF space, not on the triangle mesh. This removes terracing while keeping the overall form.
  • The Taubin step is short and optional. Heavy smoothing belongs in SDF space, not on the mesh.

docs.title: finalize_mesh(carved_grid, grid_origin, settings, voxel_size)
docs.text:
Convert carved voxels to a mesh and clean results.

Behavior

• If apply_smoothing is False: prune_voxels_morph (small-component prune + neighbour-count filter), cubic meshing, then cleanup_mesh in light mode. • If apply_smoothing is True: prune_voxels (small-component prune), SDF presmooth + marching cubes, vertex weld, then cleanup_mesh (light mode when the welded mesh is watertight), then polish_mesh_taubin with settings.smooth_iters (0 to 6).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default carved_grid Tensor(D, D, D)

Binary occupancy after carving.

required grid_origin ndarray(3)

World-space min corner for index (0,0,0).

required settings ExportingSettings

Supplies apply_smoothing, min_voxels, min_face_count and smooth_iters.

required voxel_size float

Edge length of a voxel in meters; it belongs to the preprocessing run that built the grid, so it is not part of the exporting settings.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description cleaned_voxels Tensor(D, D, D)

Post-pruned (and possibly morphologically cleaned) occupancy.

initial_mesh Trimesh

Mesh directly from the selected meshing path (pre-cleanup copy).

final_mesh Trimesh

Cleaned mesh, Taubin-polished on the smoothed path when smooth_iters > 0.

docs.text:
Remove connected components smaller than min_voxels (26-connectivity).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default voxels (D, D, D) uint8/bool torch.Tensor required min_voxels int

Size threshold; components with fewer voxels are removed.

Notes

docs.title: prune_voxels_morph(voxels, min_voxels)
docs.text:
Light cleanup for the cubic (unsmoothed) path.

Steps
  1. Remove connected components (26-connectivity) with fewer than min_voxels voxels.
  2. Remove occupied voxels whose 3×3×3 neighbourhood (including the voxel itself) holds fewer than 3 occupied voxels, i.e. voxels with 0 or 1 occupied neighbours. This drops isolated specks and one-voxel spurs.

Only removes voxels, never adds them: adding would undo carving.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default voxels (D, D, D) uint8/bool torch.Tensor required min_voxels int

Size threshold; components with fewer voxels are removed.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description cleaned (D, D, D) uint8 torch.Tensor

Binary occupancy on the same device as voxels.

docs.title: polish_mesh_taubin(mesh, iters=2)
docs.text:
Apply a short Taubin smoothing pass to remove small ripples.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh Trimesh

Modified in place.

required iters int

Number of trimesh Taubin steps, capped at 6. trimesh alternates steps (even steps shrink, odd steps inflate), so even values give complete shrink/inflate pairs. If 0 or less, the mesh is returned unchanged.

2

Returns:

Name Type Description mesh Trimesh

The same object, smoothed, with degenerate faces removed.

Notes
  • Uses fixed parameters λ = 0.28 and ν = 0.31 (trimesh's sign convention; μ = −0.31 in Taubin's notation).
  • Vertices are centred and scaled to unit median edge length during smoothing, then restored.
  • Intended only after the SDF + marching cubes path. Keep the iteration count small to avoid shape drift.

Repair and prune small fragments from a mesh.

Modified in place.

If True, skip the repair steps (fix_winding, fix_normals, fix_inversion, fill_holes, merge_vertices). Use for meshes that already have shared vertices and consistent outward winding: the cubic mesher's output and watertight marching-cubes output. Roughly 10x faster on large meshes.

docs.title: I/O
docs.text:
Mesh loading and saving through Trimesh.

  • load_mesh reads a mesh file (PLY, OBJ, STL and the other formats Trimesh supports).
  • save_mesh writes a mesh; for PLY it switches to double-precision vertices when float32 would round the coordinates (georeferenced models far from the origin).
  • validate_inputs checks that the files a preprocessing run needs exist (meshes, and the EPW for the modes that read one).
  • load_meshes loads the maximum volume and the test surfaces, and reports coordinates that a float32 PLY file has rounded.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.io
docs.text:
Mesh file input and output, and the preprocessing inputs.

load_mesh reads a mesh file (PLY, OBJ, STL...) into a trimesh mesh; save_mesh writes one, switching PLY to double-precision vertices when float32 would round georeferenced coordinates. validate_inputs checks that the files a preprocessing run needs exist, and load_meshes loads the maximum volume and the test surfaces, reporting coordinates that a float32 file has rounded; load_optional_mesh loads the optional context and terrain meshes.

docs.title: load_mesh(path, fix_normals=True)
docs.text:
Load a triangle mesh from file.

trimesh's default processing on load removes NaN/inf vertices and merges duplicate vertices; it does not fix winding or remove degenerate faces. fix_normals is then called: it makes the face winding consistent across connected faces, and for watertight meshes it also turns each closed body that is stored inside out so its normals point outward. With fix_normals False that step is left out (for meshes whose face orientation nothing reads, such as context and terrain: it takes seconds on large meshes).

Raises:

Type Description InputError

If path is not a file, if trimesh cannot parse it, or if it has no triangles (empty, or only points or curves). Without the last check the problem would only show up later as an empty voxel grid.

docs.title: load_optional_mesh(path, name)
docs.text:
Load an optional input mesh (context, terrain), or None when there is none.

No path gives None. A file without triangles counts as absent: it is reported as a <name>_empty issue and gives None, so the run behaves as without it. A missing or unreadable file raises InputError. The faces are kept as stored: neither the column rule nor the ray test reads their orientation, and fixing it takes seconds on large meshes.

docs.title: float32_resolution(coords)
docs.text: Spacing between adjacent float32 values at the largest |coordinate|.

docs.title: save_mesh(mesh, path)
docs.text:
Save a mesh to disk, creating the output directory if needed, and return the absolute file path.

The format follows the file extension. PLY is written with float64 vertices when float32 spacing at the largest coordinate exceeds 1 mm (as with georeferenced coordinates), and GLB with its offset in the node (save_glb); otherwise trimesh's exporter is used. STL can only hold float32 vertices, so a float32_coordinates issue is reported when that rounds them by more than 1 mm.

docs.title: save_glb(named_meshes, path)
docs.text:
Write the (name, mesh) pairs as one GLB scene, one node each (a name of None lets trimesh name it).

glTF stores vertices as float32, which rounds georeferenced coordinates by up to half a metre; every mesh is therefore moved by the same whole-metre offset near the scene's lowest corner, and each node's translation, a double in the file's JSON, moves it back, so readers place the vertices exactly.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
USC runs in three stages: preprocessing, thresholding, exporting, with massing as an optional fourth that reads the thresholding output like exporting. Each stage writes a manifest, last, after all its other outputs; the next stage reads it, so you can re-run thresholding with different parameters without recomputing scores. Every manifest has a random run_id, new on every run of its stage, and every manifest after preprocessing records the run_id of the manifest it was built from (upstream_run_id); a stage refuses an upstream that was re-run since (StageChainError). Manifests store paths relative to their own folder, so a run folder can be moved or copied. A stage first deletes the manifest and the outputs of its previous run in its folder, so a failed run leaves no manifest.

run_pipeline() runs the stages needed for what you ask it to produce, in one call. For finer control, call each stage individually.

from urbansolarcarver import load_config, run_pipeline

# One-shot: preprocessing, thresholding, exporting
result = run_pipeline(load_config("config.yaml"), out_dir="outputs")
print(result.exporting.export_path)

# Decomposed
from urbansolarcarver import preprocessing, thresholding, exporting
from pathlib import Path

cfg = load_config("config.yaml")
pre  = preprocessing(cfg, Path("outputs/preprocessing"))
thr  = thresholding(pre, cfg, Path("outputs/thresholding"))
exp  = exporting(thr, cfg, Path("outputs/exporting"))

docs.title: run_pipeline
docs.text:
run_pipeline(config, out_dir, produce=("exporting",), start_from="preprocessing", context=None, after=None) runs start_from and every later stage on the path to the stages in produce. Each stage writes into <out_dir>/<stage>; a stage before start_from is not run, and the next stage reads its output from its folder in out_dir.

# Floor plates as well as the mesh: preprocessing and thresholding run once
result = run_pipeline(cfg, "outputs", produce=["exporting", "massing"])
print(result.exporting.export_path, result.massing.plates_path)

# Change a threshold setting and reuse the scores already in outputs/preprocessing
cfg = load_config("config.yaml", ["carve_fraction=0.5"])
result = run_pipeline(cfg, "outputs", start_from="thresholding")
assert result.preprocessing is None   # it did not run in this call

The PipelineResult has one attribute per stage (preprocessing, thresholding, exporting, massing): the Result of a stage that ran in this call, None for the others. Its issues are the conditions noticed during the call (see Issues and run context). A start_from stage that is not on the path to a produced stage raises ValueError; a missing or stale upstream output raises StageChainError. after is given to the thresholding stage as its after (see Thresholding).

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.api
docs.text:
Public API: the pipeline stages, the run_pipeline and run_chain sequencers, and config helpers.

Importing this module imports torch, and Warp if it is installed, through api_core.

docs.title: PipelineResult(preprocessing, thresholding, exporting, massing, issues) dataclass
docs.text:
What one :func:run_pipeline call produced.

Each stage attribute holds the Result of a stage that ran in this call and is None for a stage that did not. issues are the conditions reported during the call, from all stages, in the order they were noticed.

docs.title: run_pipeline(config, out_dir, produce=('exporting',), start_from='preprocessing', context=None, after=None)
docs.text:
Run the stages needed to produce produce, one after the other.

Each stage writes into out_dir/<stage>. The sequencer runs start_from and every later stage on the path to a produced stage: preprocessing and thresholding come before exporting and massing, and producing both exporting and massing thresholds once. A stage before start_from is not run; the stage after it reads the existing output in out_dir/<stage>.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default config user_config | str | Path

A validated config, or the path of a YAML config file.

required out_dir str | Path

The run folder that holds one subfolder per stage.

required produce iterable of str

Stages wanted: any of "preprocessing", "thresholding", "exporting", "massing".

('exporting',) start_from str

The first stage to run; it must be on the path to a produced stage.

'preprocessing' context RunContext | None

Progress callback and cancel flag for the run. Without one, a context that also forwards issues to warnings is created.

None after ThresholdingResult | str | Path | None

The previous criterion's thresholding result, folder or manifest, given to the thresholding stage as its after (see :func:thresholding).

None

Returns:

Type Description PipelineResult

The Result of each stage that ran (None for the others) and the issues of the call.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If produce is empty or names an unknown stage, or start_from is not on the path to a produced stage.

StageChainError

If the stage before start_from has no usable output in out_dir.

RunCancelled

If the context is cancelled; stages that finished keep their output.

docs.title: run_chain
docs.text: run_chain(chain, out_dir=None, produce=("exporting",), start_from="preprocessing", context=None, trace=None, threshold_from=None) runs the criteria of a chain file in order on one voxel grid, then exporting and massing from the last (see Criteria). chain is a path or a ChainConfig from load_chain. Each criterion's stages write to <out_dir>/criteria/<id>/<stage>, and a criterion's thresholding takes the previous criterion's as after. It returns a ChainResult: one PipelineResult per criterion in criteria, then exporting, massing and the issues of the call. With trace (ids of criteria), only those criteria run preprocessing again and the others read their existing preprocessing folder; every criterion from the first traced one on is thresholded again. With threshold_from (an id of the chain), thresholding starts at the earlier of that criterion and the first traced one; the earlier criterion's preprocessing is read as it is. With start_from="thresholding", every criterion is thresholded again unless threshold_from is given: thresholding then starts at that criterion, and the criteria before it keep their thresholding folders, which the criterion decides after (StageChainError naming the folder when one is missing).

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.api_core.chain
docs.text: run_chain: criteria carved in sequence on one voxel grid, then exporting and massing from the last.

docs.title: ChainResult(criteria, exporting, massing, issues) dataclass
docs.text:
What one :func:run_chain call produced.

criteria has one :class:~urbansolarcarver.PipelineResult per criterion, in order, holding the preprocessing and thresholding Results of the stages that ran in this call (None for a stage that did not) and the issues reported while that criterion ran. exporting and massing are built from the last criterion and are None when they were not produced. issues are all the issues of the call, in the order they were noticed.

docs.title: run_chain(chain, out_dir=None, produce=('exporting',), start_from='preprocessing', context=None, trace=None, threshold_from=None)
docs.text:
Carve the criteria of chain one after the other on one voxel grid, then build from the last.

Criterion <id> runs preprocessing into out_dir/criteria/<id>/preprocessing and thresholding into out_dir/criteria/<id>/thresholding, deciding only among the voxels the previous criterion kept. Exporting and massing read the last criterion's thresholding and write out_dir/exporting and out_dir/massing, with the settings the criteria share. out_dir/criteria/chain.json lists the criteria and the thresholding run of each, and the run report has a "Criteria" section.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default chain ChainConfig | str | Path

A loaded chain, or the path of a YAML file with a criteria: list.

required out_dir str | Path | None

The run folder. Default: the out_dir of the chain's shared settings.

None produce iterable of str

Stages wanted, as for :func:~urbansolarcarver.run_pipeline.

('exporting',) start_from str

"preprocessing" traces every criterion. "thresholding" reads each criterion's existing preprocessing folder and thresholds the chain again (from threshold_from on, when given). "exporting" and "massing" read the last criterion's existing thresholding folder.

'preprocessing' context RunContext | None

Progress callback and cancel flag for the run. Progress is reported under criterion <id> for the criteria, and the issues of a criterion's stages are named criterion <id> (<stage>). Without a context, one that also forwards issues to warnings is created.

None trace collection of str | None

With start_from="preprocessing": the ids of the criteria to trace again. The others read their existing criteria/<id>/preprocessing folder, and every criterion from the first traced one on is thresholded again (the ones before it keep their thresholding, which the first thresholded one decides after). Default: trace every criterion. Ignored for the other values of start_from.

None threshold_from str | None

With start_from="preprocessing": the id of a criterion to threshold again even when it comes before the first traced one (its preprocessing, which was not traced, is read as it is). Thresholding then starts at the earlier of this criterion and the first traced one. Default: start at the first traced criterion. With start_from="thresholding": thresholding starts at this criterion; the criteria before it keep their thresholding, which the first one thresholded decides after. Default: threshold every criterion. Ignored for the other values of start_from.

None

Returns:

Type Description ChainResult

The Results of each stage that ran (None for the others) and the issues of the call.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If produce is empty or names an unknown stage, start_from is not on the path to a produced stage, or trace names no criterion of the chain, or threshold_from names none.

StageChainError

If a folder to read before start_from (or the preprocessing folder of a criterion that trace leaves out, or of a criterion before threshold_from with start_from="thresholding") has no usable output; the message names the stage to re-run.

RunCancelled

If the context is cancelled; stages that finished keep their output.

docs.title: Deciding what to re-run
docs.text: stages_to_rerun(previous_config, new_config, produce) lists, in pipeline order, the stages that have to run to bring produce up to date after a config change. It compares the settings each stage reads (preprocessing, then thresholding, then each produced leaf stage) and does not look at input files or at which stages exist on disk; that is for the caller to decide. With no previous config it lists every stage produce needs.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.stage_settings
docs.text:
Per-stage settings projected from the flat configuration.

Each stage reads only its own settings model; RunOptions holds what does not affect results. effective_values gives the values a stage will apply (defaults resolved, fields its mode does not read left out), so two configs that mean the same compare equal, and :func:stages_to_rerun turns those comparisons into the list of stages to run.

This module must not import api_core (it pulls in torch).

docs.title: stages_to_rerun(previous_config, new_config, produce)
docs.text:
The stages to run, in pipeline order, to bring produce up to date.

Compares settings only; whether an input file changed, or whether a stage was ever run, is for the caller to decide.

  • Preprocessing effective values differ: preprocessing, thresholding and the produced leaves (exporting, massing).
  • Else thresholding differs: thresholding and the produced leaves.
  • Else each produced leaf whose own effective values differ.

Only stages that produce needs are listed, so producing "preprocessing" alone stops the list there. With no previous_config, every stage needed for produce is listed. Raises ValueError for a name that is not in :data:PIPELINE_STAGES.

docs.title: Issues and run context
docs.text:
Conditions that are not errors (settings the mode ignores, nothing carved, a footprint that could not be read, ...) are reported as issues: an Issue has the stage it was noticed in, a short code and a message. Each stage Result has issues, and PipelineResult.issues holds those of the whole call. Without a run context the engine also emits each issue as a warning.

A RunContext passed to run_pipeline collects the issues, calls on_progress(stage, done, total) as a stage advances, and stops the run when cancel() is called (RunCancelled; stages that finished keep their output). report_issue(code, message) records an issue on the active context.

from urbansolarcarver.run_context import RunContext

context = RunContext(on_progress=lambda stage, done, total: print(stage, done, total))
result = run_pipeline(cfg, "outputs", context=context)
for issue in result.issues:
    print(issue.stage, issue.code, issue.message)

Run context: collects issues, reports progress and carries cancellation.

Standard library only. A :class:RunContext is activated for a block with :func:run_context; engine code then calls :func:report_issue and :func:report_progress without passing the context around. Without an active context an issue is emitted as a warning, so direct calls to engine functions behave as before.

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text: Voxelizes the max volume, samples the test surfaces, generates rays toward sky patches (or sun positions, or the tilted-plane direction), traces them through the voxel grid, and writes per-voxel obstruction scores to scores.npy.

docs.title: PreprocessingResult(out_dir, volume_path, volume_shape, dtype, run_id, device_info='', issues=()) dataclass
docs.text:
Immutable record returned by :func:preprocessing.

Carries paths to persisted artifacts and grid metadata so that downstream stages (thresholding, exporting) can locate them without re-computation. volume_path is the scores.npy file. The manifest_path property points to the JSON manifest that the next stage reads; the object also implements __fspath__ (returning that manifest path) so it can be passed directly as a path-like to :func:thresholding.

docs.title: preprocessing(cfg, out_dir)
docs.text:
First stage of the 3-stage envelope pipeline: per-voxel obstruction scoring.

Converts a maximum-volume mesh and a set of insolation test surfaces into a 3-D scalar field where each voxel carries a score indicating how much it blocks sun or sky from the test surfaces. The steps are:

  1. Voxelization: the maximum-volume mesh is rasterized into a cubic occupancy grid with edge length cfg.voxel_size. This and the next two steps run in a local frame whose origin is the max volume's minimum corner; persisted coordinates are shifted back to world space.
  2. Surface sampling: the test surfaces are point-sampled (spacing cfg.grid_step), giving test points with outward normals. The test surface PLY file may contain several disjoint mesh components (e.g. separate facade panels, a ground plane and a courtyard, or a PV array). All components are sampled and their ray contributions added into a single score grid.

  3. Ray casting: for every test point, rays are cast through the voxel grid according to the configured mode. Each voxel that blocks a ray accumulates a weight that depends on the mode:

  4. time-based: sun-position rays for the configured analysis period; a voxel's score is the protected-surface area it shades times the duration, in m²·h (each sample point stands for ~grid_step² m²).

  5. tilted_plane: one ray per sample point at the plane angle; a non-zero score means the voxel lies on or above at least one plane.
  6. sky-patch modes (irradiance, benefit, daylight, radiative_cooling): rays go toward the sky patches, each patch carrying a mode-specific weight; a voxel's score is the sum of the weights of the rays it blocks times the area each sample point stands for (grid_step²): the solar energy it blocks in kWh (irradiance, benefit), or the sky it hides in m² of fully hidden sky (daylight, radiative_cooling; their weights sum to 1).

With the optional context (cfg.context_path) and terrain (cfg.terrain_path) meshes, step 1 also removes every voxel column the context overlaps and the voxels below the ground, and in the ray-based modes step 3 drops every ray that hits the context or the terrain before scoring (unless cfg.context_blocks_rays is off). tilted_plane loses the voxels only.
